fullPassage:
Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!

Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.

Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.

Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.

It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.

Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.

Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

det.tip: 주어가 '~되는' 대상이면 수동태 be + 과거분사 → is treated

questions.passage: Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④가 본문(기존 스캔과 비교해 일치를 찾음)과 일치
det.analysis:
① 불일치 — 손바닥 스캔으로 '더는 신용카드가 필요 없다(no longer need)'고 했어요.
② 불일치 — 정맥 패턴은 '지문과 달리(unlike fingerprints)' 몰래 채취되기 어렵다고 했어요.
③ 불일치 — '일치하는 것이 없을 때(If there are no matches)' 새 스캔이 추가돼요. 일치가 있을 때가 아니에요.
④ 일치 — 'it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches(기존 스캔과 비교해 일치를 찾는다)'와 맞아요 ←정답
det.tip: 기존 스캔과 비교해 일치 확인 → ④ 일치

ch: 손바닥 스캔을 쓰려면 여전히 신용카드가 반드시 필요하다.
손바닥 스캔은 지문처럼 본인 모르게 쉽게 채취될 수 있다.
일치하는 패턴이 있을 때 새 스캔이 데이터베이스에 추가된다.
손바닥 스캔은 정맥 패턴을 기존 스캔과 비교해 일치 여부를 확인한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② serving → serve: 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형 serve. serving(-ing)은 조동사 뒤에 올 수 없음
det.analysis:
① added — 'it is ① added to the database(추가된다)' 수동태, 적절해요.
② serving — 'these palm scans can ② serving as a digital signature(디지털 서명 역할을 할 수 있다)'에서 조동사 can 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 와요. serving(-ing)은 올 수 없고 serve로 써야 해요 → 틀려요 ←정답
③ carry — 'people no longer need to ③ carry credit cards(신용카드를 들고 다닐 필요 없다)'에서 to 뒤 동사원형 carry, 적절해요.
④ make — 'able to ④ make purchases(구매할 수 있는)'에서 to 뒤 동사원형 make, 적절해요.
det.tip: 조동사(can) 뒤에는 동사원형. serving(-ing)은 불가 → serve

questions.passage: It is now ①<u>believed</u> that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could ②<u>have</u> adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be ③<u>limiting</u> to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which ④<u>absorbs</u> greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: limiting → limited (be limited to: ~에 국한되다, 수동태이므로 과거분사)
det.analysis:
① believed: 'It is now believed that ~'는 '~라고 여겨진다'는 수동태(be + 과거분사) — 적절
② have: 'could have adverse effects' 조동사 could 뒤 동사원형 — 적절
③ limited: 'This warming would not be __________ to the desert'는 'be limited to(~에 국한되다)'라는 수동태 표현이라 과거분사 limited가 맞음. limiting은 틀림 ←정답
④ absorbs: 선행사 the dark water(단수) + 관계사절 동사 absorbs 단수 일치 — 적절
det.tip: be limited to ~ = ~에 국한되다(수동태). limiting → limited

questions.passage: Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is ①<u>saying</u> that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be ②<u>employed</u> in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study ③<u>conducted</u> in 2016 ④<u>analyzed</u> 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: saying → said (be동사 + 과거분사 수동태: It is said that ~ = ~라고 이야기된다)
det.analysis:
① saying: 'It is ___ that this is an unconscious bias'에서 It은 '말해지는' 대상이라 be동사 뒤 과거분사가 오는 수동태가 필요해요. said가 맞고 현재분사 saying은 틀려요 ←정답
② employed: 'to be employed' 수동 부정사 — 적절
③ conducted: 'A study conducted in 2016' 과거분사 후치수식 — 적절
④ analyzed: 'A study ... analyzed 14 million reviews' 주어 study의 과거시제 본동사 — 적절
det.tip: It is + 과거분사 + that ~ = ~라고 여겨진다/이야기된다(수동태). It is said that

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being ①<u>threatened</u> by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can ②<u>safely</u> live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are ③<u>silent</u>. They attract ④<u>many</u> new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: many → few: 새로운 서식 동물을 '거의 못(few)' 끌어들여 더 악화된다는 흐름
det.analysis:
① threatened: 산호초가 따뜻한 물에 위협받음 — 적절
② safely: '안전하게(safely) 살 수 있는 곳'임을 어린 물고기에게 알림 — 적절
③ silent: 손상된 산호초는 조용함(silent) — 적절
④ many → few ←정답: 'They attract ___ new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further'는 새 서식 동물을 '거의 못(few)' 끌어들여 더 악화된다는 흐름이에요. '많이(many)' 끌어들이면 악화된다는 결과와 모순되므로 few가 맞아요.
det.tip: 서식 동물이 few(거의 없음) → 더 악화. many(많이)는 결과와 모순

questions.passage: Local elementary schools are invited to join us in ①<u>mourning</u> the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The ②<u>theme</u> of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may ③<u>submit</u> only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to ④<u>announce</u> a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① mourning=애도하는 → celebrating(기념하는) ② theme=주제 ③ submit=제출하다 ④ announce=발표하다
det.analysis:
① mourning: 지하철 시스템의 25주년은 '기념하는(celebrating)' 기쁜 일이지 '애도하는(mourning)' 일이 아니므로 문맥상 부적절 ←정답

④ announce: 10월 1일까지 우승자를 '발표(announce)'하려는 흐름 — 적절
det.tip: 지하철 25주년은 '기념(celebrating)'할 일. mourning(애도)은 문맥과 반대

questions.passage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was ①<u>stronger</u> near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground ②<u>hit</u> a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which ③<u>occurs</u> when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's ④<u>different</u> to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① stronger=더 센 ② hit=치다 ③ occurs=발생하다 ④ similar→different (부적절)
det.analysis:
① stronger: 높은 건물 근처에서 바람이 더 세다 — 적절
② hit: 센 바람이 건물을 친다 — 적절
③ occurs: 통로 효과가 발생한다 — 적절
④ different: 좁은 곳의 바람이 강물의 흐름과 '다르다'? 좁을수록 빨라지는 점이 강물과 '비슷하다(similar)'는 흐름이므로 different는 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 좁을수록 빨라짐 = 강물과 similar(비슷함). different(다른)는 반대

questions.passage: Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior ①<u>tends</u> to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person ②<u>grows</u> older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about ③<u>keep</u> or ④<u>getting</u> rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: keep → keeping (전치사 about 뒤에는 동명사가 오므로 keeping)
det.analysis:
① tends: 'behavior tends to start'는 'tend to + 동사원형' 구조라 적절해요.
② grows: 'as the person grows older'에서 주어 person이 단수라 grows — 적절해요.
③ keep: 'decisions about keep or getting rid of'에서 전치사 about 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 해요. 그래서 원형 keep이 아니라 keeping이 맞아요. 뒤의 getting과 병렬로 이어져요 ←정답
④ getting: 'or getting rid of'에서 전치사 about에 이어지는 동명사라 적절해요.
det.tip: 전치사(about) 뒤 동사는 -ing(동명사). keeping or getting 병렬

questions.passage: Have you ever seen rows of ①<u>identical</u> fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look ②<u>unattractive</u>, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their ③<u>harvest</u> because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ④<u>ugly</u> produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② unattractive → pretty. 진열된 농산물은 '예뻐(pretty)' 보임
det.analysis:
① identical: 진열대에 줄지어 놓인 '똑같은(identical)' 과일 — 적절

② unattractive: 진열된 농산물이 '볼품없어(unattractive)' 보인다? 겉모습은 '예뻐(pretty)' 보이지만 그 뒤가 반전이라 pretty가 원문. 틀림 ←정답

③ harvest: 수확물(harvest)의 50%를 버림 — 적절

④ ugly: 단체들이 '못난이(ugly)' 농산물을 사들임 — 적절
